findings.explanation: api-gateway returned 62 '503 Service Unavailable' responses that name auth-service as the failing downstream (09:30:03–09:34:07 UTC). They interleave one-for-one with the auth-service validation failures, so clients saw the auth problem as gateway 503s.

findings.title: Payment gateway timeouts to Stripe
findings.explanation: payment-service logged 150 'Payment gateway timeout provider=Stripe' errors (09:58:20–10:00:49 UTC) for all 6 tenants. There are no internal exceptions or database errors in that window, which fits a provider-side problem, but the logs alone can't confirm it.

findings.title: 403 policy mismatch for tenant nike-us
findings.explanation: auth-service rejected 120 requests with 'Permission denied policy mismatch status=403' (11:13:20–11:15:19 UTC). Every one is for tenant nike-us, spread across pod-0, pod-1, pod-2 and pod-3, so the problem is scoped to that tenant rather than one pod.

findings.title: token-service retrying token refresh
findings.explanation: token-service logged 63 'Retrying token refresh' warnings (09:30:01–09:34:09 UTC), starting 1 s after its own 2.8.1 deployment. There are no retry warnings anywhere else in the file.

findings.title: search-service long GC pauses (2,500 ms)
findings.explanation: search-service logged 111 'GC pause duration=2500ms' warnings (10:48:20–10:50:10 UTC). Back-to-back pauses this long mean the JVM was spending a large share of its time collecting garbage, a typical sign of a nearly full heap.

incidents.narrative: One second after token-service logged 'Deployment completed version=2.8.1' at 09:30:00 it began retrying token refreshes. From 09:30:01 to 09:34:09 four errors repeat in a fixed cycle: the token-service retry, a db-proxy SQL timeout, an api-gateway 503 (downstream=auth-service) and an auth-service OAuth validation failure (provider_status=401). The cycle stops at 09:34:09; no rollback or restart is logged.
incidents.rootCauseHypothesis: The token-service 2.8.1 deployment is the most likely trigger: it is the only change logged before the failures, and they start 1–4 s after it. The SQL timeouts follow the same cycle, so they look like a symptom rather than the cause. Confirm by diffing 2.8.1's token-validation config against the previous release.

incidents.narrative: payment-service could not reach Stripe from 09:58:20 to 10:00:49: 150 gateway timeouts spread evenly across all 6 tenants.
incidents.rootCauseHypothesis: Provider-side latency or an outage at Stripe, since every failure is a timeout to the provider and no internal errors are logged. Check Stripe's status history for this window.

incidents.narrative: redis-cache timed out on 100 connections between 10:23:20 and 10:24:59, across all pods.
incidents.rootCauseHypothesis: A Redis availability or network problem. The logs only show client-side timeouts, so check Redis server metrics (memory, evictions, failover events) for this window.

incidents.narrative: search-service went through about two minutes of 2.5 s GC pauses (111 warnings from 10:48:20) and then failed with 49 OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space errors until 10:50:59.
incidents.rootCauseHypothesis: Heap exhaustion in search-service, from a leak or an oversized query or result set. Enable -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError and compare heap usage before 10:48:20.

incidents.narrative: For two minutes (11:13:20–11:15:19 UTC) auth-service rejected every logged request from tenant nike-us with a 403 policy mismatch, on all four pods.
incidents.rootCauseHypothesis: A tenant-level authorization policy for nike-us that no longer matches what auth-service expects, such as a policy edit or a role-mapping change. The logs don't show the change itself; check the policy store's audit log for nike-us around 11:13:20.

# Incident report: owner_sample_10k.log

## Summary
10,000 log lines from 09:00 to 11:46 UTC on 15 Jul 2026. The deterministic parsers counted 605 ERROR and 174 WARN lines; the anomaly gate flagged 16 of 167 one-minute windows, which correlate into **5 incidents**. The most severe is an auth failure cascade that began seconds after the token-service 2.8.1 deployment; the second is an OutOfMemoryError crash in search-service.

## Key Metrics
| Metric | Value | Peak minute (UTC) |
|---|---|---|
| Log lines (TRAFFIC.lines) | 10,000 | — |
| ERROR lines (ERRORS.errors) | 605 | 60 at 09:59 |
| WARN lines (LEVEL.warn_lines) | 174 | 60 at 10:49 |
| 401 responses (AUTH.auth_401) | 62 | 15 at 09:31 |
| 403 responses (AUTH.auth_403) | 120 | 60 at 11:14 |
| OutOfMemoryError (PERFORMANCE.oom) | 49 | 49 at 10:50 |
| GC pauses (PERFORMANCE.gc_pause_ms) | 111, p95 2,500 ms | 60 at 10:49 |
| Deploys (LIFECYCLE.deploys) | 1 | 1 at 09:30 |
| Windows flagged by the anomaly gate | 16 of 167 | — |

## Incidents

### 1. Auth cascade after the token-service 2.8.1 deploy (09:30:04–09:34:08 UTC)
The deploy at 09:30:00 was followed within seconds by token refresh retries (63), OAuth validation failures in auth-service (62, provider_status=401), api-gateway 503s naming auth-service as downstream (62) and db-proxy SQL timeouts at 12,000 ms (62). All four repeat in one fixed cycle until 09:34:09.

### 2. Stripe payment gateway timeouts (09:58:20–10:00:49 UTC)
150 payment timeouts with provider=Stripe across all 6 tenants, with no internal errors alongside them.

### 3. Redis connection timeouts (10:23:20–10:24:59 UTC)
100 client-side connection timeouts from redis-cache, spread across pod-0, pod-1, pod-2 and pod-3.

### 4. search-service GC storm and OutOfMemoryError (10:48:20–10:50:59 UTC)
111 GC pauses of 2,500 ms, then 49 OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space errors starting at 10:50:11.

### 5. 403 policy mismatch for tenant nike-us (11:13:20–11:15:19 UTC)
120 requests rejected with status=403, all for nike-us, spread over pod-0, pod-1, pod-2 and pod-3.

## Recommendations
- Diff token-service 2.8.1 against the previous release (token-validation config first) and gate future deploys on the auth-service 401 rate.
- Put a circuit breaker and a timeout budget on the Stripe client so checkout fails fast instead of piling up timeouts.
- search-service: enable heap dumps on OOM and alert when GC pauses exceed 1 s; this crash gave two minutes of warning.
- Alert on the per-tenant 403 rate, so a tenant-scoped policy break pages someone even when other tenants look healthy.
- Pull Redis server-side metrics for 10:23:20–10:24:59 UTC; the application logs only show the client side.

qa.question: What caused the 503 errors around 09:30?
qa.answer: The 503s came from **api-gateway**, and each one names **auth-service** as the failing downstream (62 errors, 09:30:03–09:34:07 UTC). auth-service was failing OAuth validation with `provider_status=401` (62 errors) in the same cycle. The cycle starts right after token-service logged `Deployment completed version=2.8.1` at 09:30:00, so that deploy is the most likely trigger.

qa.question: Which tenants were hit by the 403 errors?
qa.answer: Only **nike-us**. All 120 `Permission denied policy mismatch status=403` errors (11:13:20–11:15:19 UTC) are for that tenant, spread across pod-0, pod-1, pod-2 and pod-3. The log has no lines from other tenants during those two minutes, so it can't tell whether they were affected too.

qa.question: What happened before search-service ran out of memory?
qa.answer: From 10:48:20 search-service logged 111 `GC pause duration=2500ms` warnings: long, back-to-back pauses. The first `OutOfMemoryError Java heap space` comes at 10:50:11, one second after the last GC warning (10:50:10), and 49 OOM errors follow until 10:50:59. GC thrashing followed by OOM points to the heap filling up over about two minutes, not to a single bad request.

qa.question: Was Stripe at fault for the payment failures?
qa.answer: The logs can't prove it either way. All 150 errors are `Payment gateway timeout provider=Stripe` from payment-service (09:58:20–10:00:49 UTC), across all 6 tenants, with no internal exceptions or database errors in that window. That fits a provider-side problem, but confirming it needs Stripe's status history for that time.
